doc.name: a2bflight fares
doc.instructions: Flight fares from a2bflight.com, cheapest first. Every price is for one adult in economy. Each fare carries found_at, the day it was found (a row without one carries checked, the day its route was last checked); give that day with the price. Fares are shown before bags: bag fees and the final price appear at checkout on the seller's page. Quote each price in the currency its row gives: never convert it or look up an exchange rate. A one-way row may carry typical_price, the route's typical one-way fare, and pct_below_typical, how many percent below it the fare is; use both as given. Lead with the few cheapest rows rather than every row. Each row's trip says one-way or return; most travellers fly there and back, so give both when a route has both, the one-way first, and say a return's stops and duration cover both directions. Give the user the row's page_url first: it shows the whole route on a2bflight.com. book_url opens the seller's booking page for that fare. Never invent a link. Look up codes with find_airports; use cheapest_routes for where to go from a city, and route_fares for one airport pair. For a group flying from several cities, use where_to_meet to find where they can meet, or meet_link when they know where, and give the user its meet_url.

tools.description: Use this when someone asks where they can fly cheaply from a city, or for flight deals under a budget or in a month. Returns the cheapest fare on each route with fares from an origin (or into a destination), cheapest one-way first, each with its cheapest round trip of a 3 to 21 day stay in `return` when the route has one. Filter by a maximum price and a departure month here rather than by reading the list; both apply to the one-way. Prices are for one adult in economy; each fare carries found_at, the day it was found (or checked, the day its route was last checked, when it has none), and a one-way may carry typical_price and pct_below_typical.

from.description: where the flights leave from: origin IATA airport or city code (NYC covers JFK, LGA and EWR); give from, to or both

to.description: where the flights land: destination IATA airport or city code

max_price.description: keep only fares at or under this amount, in the currency the results carry

month.description: YYYY-MM: the cheapest fare departing in that month; needs from

limit.description: how many routes to return, 1 to 20; 10 when omitted

tools.description: A link to a2bflight.com's group page for people flying from different homes to meet in one place. Use it when the user already knows where; where_to_meet when they ask where. Without dates it picks the weekend, of the next eight, whose round trips cover everyone for the lowest total, and returns each fare and the total; with dates it returns no price, and the page shows each person's cheapest fare for those dates or the closest. A warning says why the fares are a poor option and what to try instead: pass it on.

home.description: the person's home IATA airport, such as JFK — an airport, not a city code

adults.description: how many adults fly from this home together; omit for 1

members.description: 2 to 8 people, each flying from their own home; person 1 first

to.description: the IATA airport where they all meet — an airport, not a city code

out.description: YYYY-MM-DD: the day they meet; leave out and back both empty for a suggested long weekend

back.description: YYYY-MM-DD: the day everyone flies home

mode.description: cheapest_total (the default: the lowest sum), fairest (the lowest dearest ticket), least_travel (the least flying time) or earliest_together (everyone landed soonest)

tools.description: Use this when someone asks about flights, flight prices, airfare or cheap plane tickets between two airports or cities (for example Seoul to Tokyo; find_airports turns a city into its airports). Returns the fares for one airport pair: the cheapest one-way, the cheapest round trip of a 3 to 21 day stay, a fare calendar of the cheapest one-way by departure date, the cheapest one-way in each month, and the cheapest round trips. A one-way may carry typical_price, the route's typical one-way fare, and pct_below_typical. When the pair has no fares yet, it looks the route up; if the fares are not back in time it answers status "pricing", and asking again a minute later reads them.

to.description: where the flight lands: destination IATA airport code

month.description: YYYY-MM: keep only departure dates in that month

tools.title: Route fares

tools.description: Where 2 to 8 people flying from different homes can meet cheapest: the places every home has a route into, each with a weekend that has a round trip for everyone, each person's fare, the total, and meet_url — the group's page with all of it filled in. A place with a warning is a poor option: say why, and offer the better pick it names. Prices are for one adult in economy; each fare carries found_at, the day it was found (or checked, the day its route was last checked, when it has none).

nights.description: nights they stay, 1 to 14; 3 (Friday to Monday) when omitted

limit.description: how many places to return, 1 to 8; 5 when omitted
